api.provider_daily_statistic: measure id suffix '-temp-m-86400-C-qualified' = EA 'Daily mean Temperature (°C) time series', period 86400 s, unitName °C, observedProperty Temperature
api.day_definition: one value per calendar date; reading payload carries date (YYYY-MM-DD) and dateTime (T00:00:00, no offset) = the provider's daily mean for that calendar day in UK local time as published

caveats: Provider daily statistic only, no re-aggregation: the accepted series are the EA 'Daily mean Temperature (°C)' measures (period 86400 s). The daily min/max measures and the 15-minute instantaneous series are not used to build panels; a derived daily mean from the 15-minute series is written to derived_subdaily_vs_provider_daily.csv as QC evidence only, because protocol rule 3 requires the provider's own daily statistic.

Coverage is small and this is the central caveat: of 2012 temperature measures in the live EA catalogue, only 16 are provider daily means, covering 16 hydrometric stations. Temperature measure kinds: event_monitor_subdaily_900s=1926, provider_daily_min_or_max_86400s=32, other_named_monitor_subdaily_900s=22, hydrometric_guid_15min_instantaneous_900s=16, provider_daily_mean_86400s=16. Everything else in the temperature catalogue is sub-daily (900 s): E-code event-monitor spot series and other named monitors, which carry no daily statistic, plus the same 16 stations' daily min/max statistics.

Day boundary: the EA daily mean is published per calendar date (dateTime T00:00:00, no offset) in UK local time. The 15-minute series used in the derived QC carries local clock timestamps; no UTC conversion was applied by this ingest. The frozen endpoint (hottest-30 mean) is a summer statistic, so a one-hour DST boundary difference cannot reorder the hottest 30 days, but downstream code must not reinterpret the dates as UTC.

Missing days are blank in daily_wide_temperature.csv. The EA also publishes 'completeness', 'valid', 'invalid' and 'missing' fields per daily reading; these are cached in raw_cache/readings/<station>_daily.csv and summarised in ingest.json so a reviewer can apply a stricter completeness rule than the one used here.

Networks are a documented spatial proxy (complete-linkage on lat/lon with a 50 km maximum pairwise geodesic cap, >= 2 stations), not an EA-native catchment label: the hydrology API exposes no catchment grouping for these stations. The 100 km sensitivity grouping is written to spatial_clusters_100km_sensitivity.csv but is never emitted as panels, so no station is double counted across caps.

Complete years use the sealed definition (>= 365 days, 366 in leap years). The EA daily archive currently ends 2024-12-30, so calendar year 2024 is incomplete for every station and is excluded, which costs one otherwise complete year per station.

Automatic QC excludes only non-numeric values, values outside -5..40 degC and readings whose EA quality code is one of ['bad', 'deleted', 'invalid', 'rejected']; every accepted station records its own accepted_quality_codes in stations.csv.
No frozen-screen performance was computed on this panel: ingest + QC stops at structural eligibility, as the protocol requires.

Frozen-sensor evidence at station a473e348-c00a-46c6-a93b-921f9747f96f: 339 accepted days are exactly 0.0 degC and the longest identical run is 295 days (2017-06-06 .. 2018-03-27). The values were NOT deleted (the protocol asks for the provider's daily statistic, and a silent deletion would be a substitution); the station is flagged in stations.csv (frozen_sensor_suspected) so the transport analysis can exclude it explicitly.

Frozen-sensor evidence at station f8ae6b4c-56c4-45a1-b83f-4697843b937f: 13 accepted days are exactly 0.0 degC and the longest identical run is 13 days (2019-07-27 .. 2019-08-08). The values were NOT deleted (the protocol asks for the provider's daily statistic, and a silent deletion would be a substitution); the station is flagged in stations.csv (frozen_sensor_suspected) so the transport analysis can exclude it explicitly.

Frozen-run sensitivity for a473e348-c00a-46c6-a93b-921f9747f96f: dropping the 295-day run (2017-06-06 .. 2018-03-27) would take complete years from 7 to 6 (lost: 2017); see results/wrr_submission_ready/multi_agency_ingest/uk_ea/frozen_sensor_sensitivity.csv

Frozen-run sensitivity for f8ae6b4c-56c4-45a1-b83f-4697843b937f: dropping the 13-day run (2019-07-27 .. 2019-08-08) would take complete years from 6 to 5 (lost: 2019); see results/wrr_submission_ready/multi_agency_ingest/uk_ea/frozen_sensor_sensitivity.csv

Under-delivery: only 2 network(s) survive the >= 2 stations with >= 4 complete years rule, far below the 30-network panel target. This is reported as under-delivery, not repaired by loosening the rule.

existing_catalog_check.note: the existing catalog is not trusted as evidence: liveness and the daily-statistic claim were re-verified against the live measures collection and per-station documents

river_only_filter.policy: station is dropped when its label, riverName or EA type list marks coastal, estuary, groundwater, lake, reservoir

derived_subdaily_qc.note: uk_ea_daily (module) derived daily means from the 15-minute series, compared with the provider's own daily mean for the same calendar days. Derived values are NOT emitted as transport networks (protocol rule 3).

frozen_sensor_census.policy: runs of identical consecutive accepted daily values are reported, not deleted: the provider value is emitted and stations.csv carries longest_identical_run_days / frozen_sensor_suspected so a downstream step can exclude the station explicitly

panel_construction.panel_index: each network panel is trimmed to the rows where at least one member station has a QC-passing value, so first_date/last_date/n_days describe the network, not the global cross-station index
panel_construction.provider_missing_rows: the EA daily readings include explicit no-data rows (provider_quality='Missing', value null, completeness='Incomplete'); they are dropped as 'provider_marked_missing_day' and counted per station in qc_ledger.csv
